newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary govt-NBH debt swap seen in mid-February.
newsitem.headline: Hungary govt-NBH debt swap seen in mid-February.

text.p: A technical debt swap between Hungary's government and the Central Bank (NBH) will be done next month, the NBH said on Friday.
"The debt swap will probably happen in mid-February, once the bank's 1996 balance is done," an NBH source told Reuters on Friday.
The cabinet approved on Thursday a plan for the central budget to repay 1,752 billion worth of forint debts to the NBH and then take up the same amount in foreign currencies.
Under the previous system, the NBH took up Hungary's foreign loans in foreign currencies and lent them on to the central state budget in forints.
"The change will reduce the NBH's losses incurred due to forint revaluation," government spokesman Elemer Kiss said on Thursday.
He added that in the future the NBH will only act as the government's agent in taking up foreign currency loans, rather than taking them up itself.
Hungary's Finance Ministry announced the plans last September, saying that the new accounting method would make the central budget more transparent.

The ministry then said it expects the debt swap to amount to some 2,000 billion forints, and the present smaller figure was a result of better-than-expected macroeconomic processes, the government said on Thursday.
Under the new system the NBH will lend limited funds to the state only if the Treasury has temporary liquidity difficulties.
